;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**According to Afghan officials, a [[United States|US]] drone strike kills more than 30 pine nut [[farmworker|farm worker]]s in [[Nangarhar Province]]. The US military say they targeted [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] terrorists. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attack-drones/u-s-drone-strike-kills-30-pine-nut-farm-workers-in-afghanistan-idUSKBN1W40NW (Reuters)]
**[[2019 Qalat bombing]]
***According to Afghan officials, a [[Taliban]] truck bomb outside a [[hospital]] in [[Qalati Ghilji|Qalat]], [[Zabul Province]], kills 39 people. The Taliban say they targeted a [[National Directorate of Security]] building nearby. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2019/09/killed-car-bomb-attack-afghan-province-zabul-190919042138106.html (Al Jazeera)]
;Business and economy
*A German magazine reports that the [[chief financial officer]] of automobile manufacturer [[BMW]], Nicolas Peter, plans to cut between 5,000 and 6,000 jobs at that company, mostly at the [[Munich]] headquarters, before 2022. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bmw-jobs/bmw-cfo-wants-to-cut-5000-6000-jobs-by-2022-manager-magazin-idUSKBN1W41XG (Reuters)]
*[[UK]]-based travel agent [[Thomas_Cook_Group|Thomas Cook]] is reported to be attempting to sell assets as it seeks to prevent its collapse. The group employs 20,000 people and, were it to collapse, approximately 150,000 British customers currently abroad could require repatriation assistance from the [[UK Civil Aviation Authority|Civil Aviation Authority]] in the largest peacetime operation of its kind. [https://news.sky.com/story/thomas-cook-seeks-last-ditch-fire-sale-in-bid-to-avert-collapse-11814043 (Sky News)]
*Over the last three days, the [[Federal Reserve Bank of New York]] adds more than [[US$]]200 billion liquidity to the [[money market]], countering a spike in the [[Repurchase agreement|repo]] rate on Tuesday. [https://www.businesslive.co.za/bd/world/americas/2019-09-19-federal-reserve-adds-third-dose-of-liquidity-to-money-market/ (''Business Day'')]
;Disasters and accidents
**An [[General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon|F-16]] [[fighter jet]] of the [[Belgian Air Component]] strikes a house before crashing into a field near [[Pluvigner]], north-west [[France]]. Both pilots eject and escape with minor injuries, but one gets his parachute entangled in high-voltage power lines, requiring two hours to rescue. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-49751536 (BBC News)]
;International relations
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**[[France]] and [[Italy]] call for a new system to redistribute immigrants to the [[European Union]] amid an ongoing increase in the numbers arriving, complaining of unfair demands being placed upon nations where immigrants make landfall. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-49752380 (BBC News)]
*[[Austria]]n MPs vote to demand a government veto on a proposed trade deal between the [[European Union]] and [[South America]]n trade group [[Mercosur]]. The deal is the result of 20 years of negotiations. [[France]] and [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] have previously threatened to also veto the deal unless Mercosur member [[Brazil]] increases efforts to fight [[2019 Amazon rainforest wildfires|ongoing Amazon rainforest wildfires]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-49753210 (BBC News)]
*The [[United States Department of State]] withholds [[US$]]160 million in direct aid to [[Afghanistan]], citing "[[Government of Afghanistan|Afghan Government]] corruption and financial mismanagement." [https://thehill.com/policy/international/462194-us-to-withdraw-and-withhold-160-million-from-afghanistan-over-corruption (''The Hill'')]
*Citing "influence operations against the United States," the US expels two [[Cuba]]n diplomats at the [[United Nations]]. [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Cuba)|Cuban Minister of Foreign Affairs]] [[Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla]] dismisses the accusations as "vulgar slander." [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/09/19/politics/us-cuba-un-diplomats/index.html (CNN)]
;Law and crime
*[[Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster|Fukushima nuclear disaster]]
**The only prosecution concerning the 2011 [[Nuclear and radiation accidents and incidents|nuclear catastrophe]] ends with the acquittal of three former [[Tokyo Electric Power Company|Tepco]] executives. The decision means nobody has been held criminally responsible for the [[nuclear meltdown|meltdown]]. [[Greenpeace]] says the verdict is not very surprising, since the case was "hugely political". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/09/japan-court-set-rule-fukushima-disaster-trial-190919000654856.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Interpol]] reports that in six weeks it has detected more than a dozen people wanted for terrorism offences crossing the [[Mediterranean Sea]] using tourist routes. The joint operation involved [[Algeria]], [[France]], [[Italy]], [[Morocco]], [[Spain]], and [[Tunisia]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-49758650 (BBC News)]
*[[Brexit]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the United Kingdom|UK Supreme Court]] finishes hearing arguments on  the lawfulness of [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]]'s [[Prorogation in the United Kingdom#Boris Johnson (2019)|prorogation]] of [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|Parliament]]. The court states it expects to rule next week. It is jointly considering appeals against two rulings. One, made by the [[High Court of Justice|High Court]] in [[London]] under [[English law]], ruled prorogation was an entirely political decision over which courts had no jurisdiction. The other, made by the [[Court of Session]] in [[Edinburgh]] under [[Scots law]], ruled Johnson acted unlawfully and the prorogation was a nullity that must be reversed. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/uk-politics-49751323 (BBC News)]
*[[Hwaseong serial murders]]
**Police in [[South Korea]] link convicted murderer Lee Chun-jae to the serial rapes and murders, which occurred between 1986 and 1991 and left ten dead. The investigations inspired the movie ''[[Memories of Murder]]'' and saw 21,000 people investigated. Lee, who is serving life for the 1994 rape and murder of his sister in law, cannot be prosecuted despite a [[DNA]] link to three victims because the [[statute of limitations]] has expired. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-49750184 (BBC News)]
;Science and technology
*[[Havana syndrome]]
**A study ordered by the [[Government of Canada|Canadian government]] finds that exposure to anti-mosquito [[fumigation]], which contains [[cholinesterase]]-inhibiting [[neurotoxin]]s, coincides with brain damage causing the same symptoms as those associated with the syndrome. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-cuba-diplomats-canada/neurotoxin-may-have-caused-diplomats-illness-in-cuba-study-idUSKBN1W42QU (Reuters)]
